description: Reference drug pairs for the interaction-checker benchmark. Every pair is taken from the text of a US FDA prescribing label, retrieved through the openFDA drug label API.
source: US FDA prescription drug labels (openFDA drug label API; the same labels are published on DailyMed)

definitions.interacting: The cited label describes an interaction between the two drugs: a change in drug levels, a dose limit, a warning, or a contraindication.
definitions.non_interacting: The cited label states that a study found no interaction, or no clinically significant interaction, between the two drugs. It is a statement by that one label, not proof that no reference lists any interaction.

selectionRules: V0 pairs (P001-P065): both drugs have a single-ingredient catalogue product that the checker resolves.

V3 pairs (P066 onwards): chosen from label text without regard to whether the checker can resolve the drugs. They include drugs with no resolvable catalogue product (for example warfarin, simvastatin) and drugs absent from the checker reference data (for example lithium, valproate, dabigatran, insulin).
Pairs were chosen from label text before the checker was run on any of them.
A pair was dropped when labels disagree or a label contradicts itself (for example divalproex with carbamazepine, montelukast with warfarin, apixaban with aspirin).
A label that reports no pharmacokinetic change but warns of a pharmacodynamic effect (for example bleeding or hypoglycemia) is recorded as interacting.
basis is a paraphrase of the label, not a quotation.
